# Generated File Governance

## Generation-first template discipline (RFC-0078)

When a package generates multi-line boilerplate files into `apps/*`, the generation source code must **not** contain inline string literals longer than a single line. Instead:

1. Store templates as separate files under `<package>/src/templates/<generator-name>/`.
2. Name each template file to mirror the **target path inside the app** (e.g., `src/pages/index.astro.template`, `tools/kernel.config.ts.template`).
3. Use a minimal token syntax (`{{TOKEN}}`) for per-app substitutions.
4. Read templates with `readFileSync` and apply tokens via `replace` at runtime.

This keeps generators maintainable, diff-friendly, and makes it obvious which generated file each template corresponds to. Agents must follow this rule for all new boilerplate generators and must refactor existing inline builders when substantially editing them.

## Generated-file governance protocol (RFC-0081)

All generators that write files into `apps/*` use a single unified marker:

```
GENERATED. Do not change this line unless the file contains project specific changes.
```

The marker is comment-syntax-aware per file type:

- `// GENERATED...` for `.ts`, `.mjs`, `.js`
- `<!-- GENERATED... -->` for `.md`
- `/* GENERATED... */` for `.css`
- `# GENERATED...` for `.yml`, `.txt`, `_headers`

**Protocol:**

- File carries the marker → generator overwrites it on every run.
- File lacks the marker → generator skips it (considered customized).
- AI agents must never edit a file that carries this marker.

**Generator ownership.** Many files under `apps/*` are generated by commands, templates, and codegen utilities owned by `packages/*`. Treat marked generated files as outputs, not authoritative editable sources. This includes app-scoped instruction files such as `apps/<site>/AGENTS.md` when they carry the marker.

To change generated output, agents must:

1. Identify the owning generator, template, or codegen package under `packages/*`.
2. Modify the generator source or template instead of the generated app file.
3. Regenerate the affected files with the appropriate `pnpm` / `site-kernel` command.
4. Run the relevant validation for the affected app or package.

Only remove the marker when an explicit task intentionally converts a file to project-specific, manually maintained ownership; document why the file is no longer generator-owned.

**RFC-0375: Two marker categories.** Generated files are now classified into two categories:

- **Category A (embedded)** — files under `src/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `tools/**` that carry the `GENERATED_MARKER` in-file. Detected by `hasGeneratedMarker(content)`. Validated by `generated.marker.validate` and guarded by `generated.edit.guard` (GEN-EDIT-01/02).
- **Category B (registry-only)** — files under `public/**` and binary outputs (PNG, ICO, SVG, WebP, MP4, WebM) that no longer carry an in-file marker. Identified solely via `GENERATOR_OWNERSHIP_MAP` entries with `markerPolicy: "registry-only"`. Validated by `generated.files.validate` (existence check) and guarded by `generated.edit.guard` (owner-module resolution via the `module` field).

**Agent lookup (RFC-0375).** Use `generated.file.lookup --path <path> [--site <app>]` to resolve any file to its generation metadata (generated, category, ownerCommand, regenerateCommand, editInstead, detectionMethod, module). Use `--diff` for batch lookup of all changed files in the git diff.

The shared constant `GENERATED_MARKER` and detector `hasGeneratedMarker(content)` live in `@gogol/site-kernel` (re-exported via `@gogol/site-kernel-codegen`). This single marker replaces all previous variants (`GENERATED BY`, `AUTO-GENERATED`, etc.). Old-marker files are treated as unmarked (skipped by generators). To migrate an old-marker file to the new protocol, update its first line and re-run the generator.

**Technical enforcement (RFC-0336, RFC-0375).** The protocol above is no longer prose-only:

- **`.gitattributes` marking.** Root `.gitattributes` carries a machine-managed `# BEGIN generated-artifacts` … `# END generated-artifacts` block marking every registry-derived generated path `linguist-generated=true`, so GitHub collapses generated diffs and excludes them from language stats. The block is produced by `gitattributes.generate` from `docs/command-manifest.generated.yaml` `writes` globs and `GENERATOR_OWNERSHIP_MAP` — **never hand-edit the block or the pattern list**; run `pnpm exec site-kernel run gitattributes.generate` after registering a new generator's outputs. `gitattributes.validate` (in `packages.check`) fails on drift (`GITATTR-01`), warns on an unsorted-but-correct block (`GITATTR-02`), and warns when a tracked marker-carrying file has no covering pattern (`GITATTR-03`).
- **Advisory header (Category A only).** The single-line marker is wrapped in a richer, comment-syntax-aware block built by `buildGeneratedHeader(...)` (also in `@gogol/site-kernel`, re-exported via `@gogol/site-kernel-codegen`): a "DO NOT EDIT" line, the owner command, an "Edit instead: `<template-or-source-path>`" line, and the exact regenerate command. The first line is still the plain `GENERATED_MARKER` string, so detection is unchanged. Generators adopt the helper incrementally — the block appears on a file the next time its generator runs, not via a mass rewrite. `kernel.wire`'s whole `tools/` family (`kernel.config.ts`, `tools/modules/*.ts`, `tools/runtime/*.ts`) already uses it; use it for any new or substantially-edited generator. **Category B files do not emit this header** — their ownership is tracked solely via `GENERATOR_OWNERSHIP_MAP`.
- **`generated.edit.guard`.** Fails when a generated file changed without its owner changing in the same range (`GEN-EDIT-01`), or the marker was removed without a documented exemption (`GEN-EDIT-02`, Category A only). For Category A, it reads the file's own "Edit instead:" line to find its owner. For Category B, it resolves the owner via the `module` field in `GENERATOR_OWNERSHIP_MAP`. Binary files that are deleted and recreated (status `A`/`D` in `git diff --name-status`) are exempt from `GEN-EDIT-01` as regenerations. Runs as its own CI job (`.github/workflows/generated-edit-guard.yml`), mirroring `commit.message.lint`, and locally defaults to the working-tree change set. If it fires, edit the named owner and regenerate — never silence it by deleting the marker.
- **`generated.marker.validate` (Category A only).** Checks that expected Category A files carry the `GENERATED_MARKER`. Category B files are excluded — their existence is checked by `generated.files.validate` instead.
- **`generated.files.validate` (RFC-0375).** Checks that every registry-declared generated file in `GENERATOR_OWNERSHIP_MAP` exists on disk. Covers both Category A and Category B. Runs in `build.prepare` and `apps.check.author` pipelines.
- **`generated.file.lookup` (RFC-0375).** Agent-facing command for resolving file paths to generation metadata. Supports `--path` for single lookup and `--diff` for batch lookup of changed files.

**For future commands:** any command that writes generated output MUST keep its `writes` globs (RFC-0266) and, for `apps/*` outputs, its `GENERATOR_OWNERSHIP_MAP` entry (RFC-0087) accurate, then run `gitattributes.generate` so the new outputs are marked automatically. For Category A files, emit the marker via `buildGeneratedHeader(...)`. For Category B files (`public/**` and binary outputs), set `markerPolicy: "registry-only"` and `module` in the `GENERATOR_OWNERSHIP_MAP` entry — do not emit a marker.

## Content-driven generation contract (RFC-0087)

Every generator that writes files into `apps/*` must satisfy three invariants:

1. **Single owner** — every generated file must be written by exactly one kernel command. The `generator.ownership.lint` command in `@gogol/site-kernel-checks` enforces this via a static `GENERATOR_OWNERSHIP_MAP`. When adding a new generator, register all its output paths in that map.
2. **Content-driven** — generator output must derive from `src/content/system.md` properties (routes, domain, languages, biome). No hardcoded constants or separate config files. Use `getDomainFromManifest()` for the canonical domain, `getSupportedLanguages()` / `getDefaultLanguage()` for i18n, and `getBiomeDisplayName()` for the biome.
3. **Idempotent** — re-running any generator must produce identical output. The `writeManagedFile()` function enforces this: identical content returns `"unchanged"` (zero file writes). For Category A files, files without the `GENERATED_MARKER` are skipped to preserve project-specific edits. For Category B files, the output is always overwritten (no marker to check).

These invariants are enforced by the `generator.ownership.lint` command (in `PACKAGES_CHECK_PIPELINE`) and the `pnpm --filter @gogol/site-kernel-codegen test` suite.

**Parallel-safe (RFC-0258).** Any kernel command that writes a file outside its target app directory — the workspace root, `docs/`, or `packages/ontology/` — must write through `writeFileAtomic` from `@gogol/site-kernel` (temp file in the same directory, then atomic rename) instead of a raw `node:fs` `writeFile`/`writeFileSync`, and must be declared on the static `SHARED_WRITE_ALLOWLIST` in `packages/os/site-kernel-checks/src/workspace-write-boundary.ts`. `turbo run build` runs app builds in parallel, so an unprotected shared writer can be caught mid-write by a concurrent reader; atomic rename plus the allowlist keep these writes torn-file-safe without cross-process locks. Enforced by `workspace.write.boundary.lint` (`WS-WRITE-01`/`WS-WRITE-02`, fail-hard in `PACKAGES_CHECK_PIPELINE`).

## YAML-only contract for generated artifacts and project configs (RFC-0376)

All generated artifacts and project configuration/state files use `.yaml` extension. JSON is reserved exclusively for tool-mandatory files that external tools require (npm, TypeScript, Turborepo, Cloudflare, MCP, VS Code, etc.).

- **Generated artifacts** use `.generated.yaml` extension with `#` comment-based advisory headers via `buildGeneratedHeader()`. Do not use field-based advisory objects.
- **Project configs and state files** use `.yaml` extension (fleet, service configs, integration shards, surface states, provenance, etc.).
- **Tool-mandatory JSON files** (Category A) are listed in `yaml-contract.whitelist.yaml` at the repository root. Do not add JSON files outside this whitelist.
- `yaml.contract.lint` in `build.prepare` enforces the contract. Violations: `YAML-CONTRACT-01` (non-whitelist `.json`/`.jsonc`), `YAML-CONTRACT-02` (`.yml` extension — use `.yaml`), `YAML-CONTRACT-03` (`.generated.json` artifact), `YAML-CONTRACT-04` (whitelist missing or unparseable).
- Use `.yaml` extension, not `.yml`.
- Use `yaml` (Eemeli AY) library for all YAML serialization and deserialization. Do not introduce `js-yaml` or other YAML libraries.
- For generated YAML files, use `buildGeneratedHeader({ filePath: "….generated.yaml", … })` to emit the advisory block.
- When adding a new tool-mandatory JSON file, add it to `yaml-contract.whitelist.yaml` in the appropriate category.

## YAML quoting policy (RFC-0493)

All `.yaml` files in the repository must parse successfully and follow a canonical quoting style: **plain scalars by default, double quotes when needed, never single quotes**.

### Parse validation

- `yaml.parse.validate` in `build.prepare` (after `yaml.contract.lint`) and `packages.check` parse-checks all `.yaml` files using the `yaml` (Eemeli AY) library.
- `YAML-PARSE-01` (error): file failed to parse — syntax errors (bad indentation, unclosed flow collections, invalid block scalars).
- `YAML-PARSE-02` (error): file has duplicate mapping keys — silently overwrites values in many parsers.

### Quoting decision algorithm

```
1. Is the value a non-string type (boolean, number, null, date)?
   → Write it as-is (no quotes). YAML 1.2 resolves the type.
     Examples: true, false, null, 42, 3.14, 2026-07-22

2. Is the value a string that is a valid plain scalar?
   → Write it without quotes (plain style).
     A plain scalar is valid when it does NOT:
     - start with an indicator character: ! & * ? | > @ ` # " ' % { [ ,
     - start with - : ? followed by a space
     - contain : (colon+space) anywhere
     - contain # (space+hash) anywhere (starts a comment)
     - start or end with whitespace
     - in flow context (inside {} or []), contain , [ ] { }
     Examples: backend, https://example.org, marathon-stuttgart

3. Is the value a string that is NOT a valid plain scalar?
   → Use double quotes.
     Examples: "key: value", "has # hash", "true" (string not boolean)

4. Never use single quotes.
   Double quotes support escape sequences (\n, \t, \uXXXX); single quotes do not.
```

### Quick reference

| Value                | Quoting | Reason                             |
| -------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `name: backend`      | plain   | valid plain scalar                 |
| `enabled: true`      | plain   | boolean, not string                |
| `count: 42`          | plain   | number, not string                 |
| `note: "key: value"` | double  | contains `: `                      |
| `note: "true"`       | double  | string that looks like boolean     |
| `note: 'escaped'`    | wrong   | single quotes — use double instead |

### YAML 1.2 note

In YAML 1.2 (the version this ecosystem uses), `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off` are plain strings, not booleans. They do not need quotes.

### Generated YAML

When generating YAML programmatically, build a JS/TS object and serialize it with `yaml.stringify()` from the `yaml` (Eemeli AY) library. Do not hand-compose YAML strings. Run `pnpm format` afterward to normalize style.

### ESLint enforcement

`eslint-plugin-yml` with `yml/plain-scalar: ["error", "always"]` enforces plain scalars with auto-fix. Run `pnpm lint:yaml --fix` to auto-remove unnecessary quotes.

## Relative imports — HARD RULE (RFC-0092)

Every relative `import` or `export … from` inside `packages/**/*.ts(x)` MUST end in the **on-disk extension** — `.ts` (or `.tsx` for React components). Never `.js`, never `.jsx`, never extensionless. This is one rule for **all** packages, source-consumed and build-emitting alike.

```ts
// Correct
import { foo } from "./bar.ts";
export * from "./baz/quux.ts";
import Header from "./header.tsx";

// Wrong — will fail in dev (Astro SSR / Node ESM cannot find a non-existent .js file)
import { foo } from "./bar.js";
import { foo } from "./bar";
```

Why `.ts` and not `.js`? Source-consumed packages ship their TypeScript sources directly — `package.json` `exports` point at `./src/*.ts`. Astro dev (Vite + Node SSR) loads those `.ts` files as-is and resolves relative imports against actual on-disk filenames. A `./foo.js` specifier inside `./foo.ts` resolves to a file that does not exist → `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` at request time.

The shared `tsconfig/base.json` carries `allowImportingTsExtensions: true` so `.ts` specifiers are legal everywhere. The shared `tsconfig/node-lib.json` adds `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions: true` (TS 5.7+) so build-emitting consumers (e.g. `@gogol/site-kernel-content`, `@gogol/site-kernel-checks`) automatically rewrite `.ts` → `.js` in their emitted `dist/` output. **You author `.ts` everywhere; the emit chain produces `.js` on its own. You never author `.js`.**

When `tsc` errors with `TS5097: An import path can only end with a '.ts' extension when 'allowImportingTsExtensions' is enabled`, do NOT switch the imports to `.js`. The fix is to confirm the failing package's `tsconfig.json` extends `tsconfig/base.json` (or `tsconfig/node-lib.json` if it emits) — both supply the right flags. When `astro dev` errors with `Cannot find module '…/foo.js' imported from '…/foo.ts'`, the offending import has `.js` and must become `.ts`.

Two lints enforce this in `PACKAGES_CHECK_PIPELINE`:

- `import.extensions.lint` — rejects `.js`/`.jsx`/extensionless relative imports under `packages/`.
- `tsconfig.shape.lint` — verifies the shared base configs still carry `allowImportingTsExtensions` and `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`; rejects per-package overrides that set `allowImportingTsExtensions: false`.

**Historical note**: agents have flipped this convention back and forth at least 5 times because each direction "fixes" one error while introducing the other (`.js` makes `pnpm build` pass but breaks `astro dev`; `.ts` makes `astro dev` work but breaks build-emitting consumers without the shared `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` flag). The correct resolution — `.ts` in source + `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` in the emit chain — satisfies both, and the two lints above prevent regression in either direction. Do NOT split this into a per-package-type rule; there is a single convention.

## Section components must render real content (RFC-0093)

`section.scaffold` emits a content-aware starter that renders the common `pageOverride` shapes (`heading`, `kicker`, `body`, `items[]`, `cards[]`, `cta`) using semantic HTML and biome tokens. **Never ship a section whose `.astro` file renders `{JSON.stringify(pageOverride)}` — that's the developer-debug stub from earlier scaffold versions, and it produces a wall of raw JSON on the rendered page.** When `section.placeholder.lint` (in `PACKAGES_CHECK_PIPELINE`) fires, replace the stub with content-aware markup before any other change. The starter handles the 80% case; customize per archetype as needed (e.g. images, geometry, third-party embeds).
